subject: Night shift: streaming chat p99 spike during peak — FastDesk outage
messages:
From: Michael Lang <michael@fastdesk.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cloudcare.io
Date: 2028-08-23T02:14:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime chat errors — 1:30–2:00 PDT spike (p99 ~18s, 500s)

Folks,

Heads up — we started seeing severe degradation on our live chat experience around 01:30 PDT. Metrics from our side: p95 stayed ~1.2s but p99 jumped to ~18s and we saw a ~6% rate of 5xx responses for the SSE stream endpoint (/v1/stream/chat). At least one customer reported messages dropping and two sessions timed out.

We routed to CloudCare and they confirmed an increase in connection backlog and spikes in response times originating from your edge. We can share logs if helpful (sending sample shortly). This is causing visible customer impact on our support center — can we get an urgent triage?

Attached: request-log-sample.json (excerpt).

Thanks,
Michael Lang\Head of Product\FastDesk
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lang <michael@fastdesk.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T02:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors — 1:30–2:00 PDT spike (p99 ~18s, 500s)

Michael — thanks for the flag and the sample. We're taking this seriously. I've looped in SRE (Rishi) and the on-call infra engineer (Dev). Initial asks while we triage:

- Dev/Rishi: please confirm whether this is a routing/backpressure issue vs. an upstream model CPU spike.
- Dev: paste 60s window logs + connection backlog from the router and any 5xx traces.
- Rishi: snapshot of autoscaler events and instance health.

Customer-facing short plan: we're going to open a dedicated incident, attempt a fast mitigation (route to fallback host pool + increase connection cap), and update every 30 minutes. Laura — can you send a short message to FastDesk acknowledging we're on it and offering an interim workaround if needed?

Evelyn
VP, Customer Reliability\Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T02:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors — initial triage

On Tue, Aug 23, 2028 at 02:14 AM Michael Lang <michael@fastdesk.ai> wrote:
> Folks,
> 
> Heads up — we started seeing severe degradation on our live chat experience around 01:30 PDT.

Triage notes (first-pass):
- Observed a ~3.8x increase in open SSE connections for FastDesk between 01:26–01:40.
- Router (edge-proxy) reported connection queueing and transient 502/504 upstream failures at 01:29:45–01:34:10.
- Downstream inference nodes show elevated CPU (90%+) and sustained GC stalls on process LLM-worker-3.
- Autoscaler triggered but new instances were slow to reach warm state; significant cold-start overhead for the large 70B variant we route to.

Attached: slo-dashboard-screenshot.png (Grafana), request-log-sample.json (from Michael).

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Rerouted 30% of FastDesk traffic to a smaller 30B-compatible model pool (reduced token processing per request).
2) Increased router upstream connection limit and bumped keepalive timeout.
3) Enabled aggressive KV-cache pinning for active sessions where safe to do so.

I'll continue to stream logs to the incident channel. If we still see >10s p99 after 15m, recommend fallback to short-polling SDK for affected customers to remove pressure from long-lived SSE lanes.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T03:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors — initial analysis and mitigation plan

Short summary: we believe the immediate driver was a combination of long-sequence chat sessions (avg token length up ~4x for a subset of FastDesk flows) and an autoscaler lag for the 70B pool. That created a sweet spot where KV cache thrashing + increased context copying pushed LLM-worker processes into high CPU and GC cycles, which cascaded back to the router as upstream 502/504s and elevated p99.

Action plan (technical):
- Hotfix to router to prefer warm-hosts and increase connection draining window (rolling out now; expected <10m).
- Force a scale-up of 70B warm pool with prewarmed WMs (manual scale for next 30 minutes).
- Short-term model downgrade policy for affected customers: route to 30B pool for new connections, keep existing sessions pinned if they are mid-dialog.
- Postmortem next steps: improve autoscaler predictive heuristics (sequence-length aware) and add a fast-cache-restore path to reduce warm-up.

I'll also coordinate a minimal code change to reduce memory copies in the kv-cache for long sequences — small patch to land within 72h.

Rishi
SRE Lead
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lang <michael@fastdesk.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T03:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors — customer update

Michael — quick update for your team: we identified a spike in long-chat sessions that overwhelmed our warm pool for the large model you are routed to. We've taken immediate steps to reduce customer impact: routed a portion of your traffic to a smaller model variant, increased connection capacity, and applied routing prioritization to warm hosts.

What you may see in the next 20 minutes:
- Intermittent reconnections as sessions migrate (we'll try to preserve conversation state).
- Reduced p99 latency expected after warm hosts stabilize; we will monitor continuously and share dashboards.

We're opening a post-incident call for later today to walk through details and planned mitigations. In the meantime, we'd like to offer a service credit for the impacted hour — I'll coordinate with billing once we confirm the window.

Thanks for patience — Laura
Customer Success Manager\Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & exec sync request — FastDesk streaming p99 spike

Team — closing the loop on the night-shift incident for FastDesk. Timeline highlights:
- 01:26–01:40 PDT: traffic surge from FastDesk produced a 3.8x connection increase; p99 peaked ~18s with a ~6% 5xx rate.
- 02:31: mitigations applied (model reroute, router connection increase, KV-pin); p99 improved to ~2.7s by 03:00 as warm pool stabilized.

Immediate follow-ups (for exec visibility):
1) Approve a short-term customer credit (Laura to confirm amount).
2) Prioritize autoscaler heuristics and a predictive warm pool feature in the next sprint — Rishi to scope.
3) Consider a product-side guardrail: circuit-breaker to gracefully degrade SSE to short-polling for grossly long sequences.

Requesting a 15-minute exec sync at 11:00 PT to review impact and approve prioritization for the warm-pool work. Please confirm availability. I'll prepare a 1-slide summary with the Grafana snapshot and key metrics.

Evelyn
VP, Customer Reliability
